correctness.rationale: Proved exact marked probability by conditioning on independent site states and parent choices. Controlled joint factors by logarithmic product estimates and a tilted independent-Bernoulli measure uniformly on compact positive scaled-age windows; used factorial moments and a small-age first-moment bound for the full PPP. The order-statistics law follows by monotone mapping. Reproducible exact enumeration matches the all-size formulas in 544 checks. Fixed p and roots/boundaries are explicitly treated; finite checks are not infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The Markov growth mechanism or full cluster-size-count chain can generate one-point expectations, but the inspected stated global laws and covariance formulas do not imply age-ordered rare singleton births. No checked global theorem claims the required uniform multivariate factorization or the nonstationary Poisson point process. A more general unstated corollary remains possible.

value.rationale: The first retained singleton in a random recursive tree lies on the parameter-dependent n^(p/(1+p)) birth scale and obeys a genuinely marked nonhomogeneous Poisson/Weibull limit, despite linearly many eventual singleton components. This reveals an age-sensitive fragmentation phenomenon not conveyed by mean-density or covariance results; the full point process also predicts joint earliest ranks.
